title: Flatness and structure-sheaf cohomology of canonical projective-bundle fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal E$ a quasi-coherent finite locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of constant positive rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and $p:\mathbf P(\mathcal E)\to S$ its canonical symmetric-algebra relative Proj [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. Then $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every $s\in S$, the residue-field fibre $\mathbf P(\mathcal E)_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and $H^1(\mathbf P(\mathcal E)_s,\mathcal O)=0$, with cohomology of the underlying abelian structure sheaf [def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback].

source.place: definition-projective-bundle, lemma-projective-space-bundle and lemma-standard-covering-projective-space; also literature/stacks-project/coherent.tex, lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring (degree zero, q=1).

proof.text: Write the positive rank as d+1. The finite-locally-free frame-cover theorem gives opens U_i covering S and isomorphisms E|U_i with the free module on ULift (Fin (d+1)). Transport these frames from restriction to tensor pullback by the existing adjunction comparison. Apply the open and free clauses of projective_bundle_quotient_geometry. Uniqueness of pullbacks identifies p inverse-image U_i, over U_i, with standard projective d-space. The standard homogeneous charts of that space are affine d-spaces. Apply affine-space smoothness on these charts and source locality to prove smoothness of projective space, then target locality on the frame cover to prove Smooth p. Smoothness gives Flat p and LocallyOfFinitePresentation p. The proved GeometricallyReduced.of_smooth gives geometrically reduced p and hence its residue-field fibres.

Choose a frame open U_i containing s. The residue-field map has singleton image {s}, so it lifts to U_i. Paste the restriction pullback square, the local projective-space isomorphism over U_i, and ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map for this lift. Pullback uniqueness gives an isomorphism from p.fiber s to projective d-space over kappa(s), with the displayed equation on structure maps. For any field K, the standard charts of projective space over K are spectra of polynomial rings, hence connected, and they share the K-point with every homogeneous coordinate equal to 1. Their union is connected. After arbitrary field-valued base change projective space is again projective space by isPullback_map, giving geometric connectedness. Transport this morphism property through the fibre isomorphism.

For the twist O(0) on projective d-space, use the existing twist-cohomology theorem: when d=1 its top cohomology vanishes at twist zero, and when d is not 1 the middle-degree vanishing applies to q=1. This includes d=0, where q=1 is above the dimension. The existing unitIsoTwistZero identifies the underlying abelian structure-sheaf H1 with this vanishing group. Structure-sheaf cohomology functoriality shows that pullback along a scheme isomorphism has inverse the pullback along its inverse. Thus it is injective, so the zero H1 of projective space transports to p.fiber s. Empty bases have no s to consider; the frame-cover smoothness proof remains valid there.

proof_origin.note: C7: complete Lean proof from the existing quotient-geometry, affine-space smoothness, projective-space base-change and twist-cohomology declarations. The only shortcut is to deduce flatness, finite presentation and geometric reducedness from smoothness of the same local polynomial charts. All helper theorems are private and proved; no new holes.

from.place: The fibre-generator lifting step of the local-normal-form argument: polynomial-chart flatness and finite presentation, geometric reducedness and connectedness of projective-space fibres, and the vanishing of their structure-sheaf H1.

lean.statement:
theorem projective_bundle_fiber_geometry (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : 0 < r) :
    let p := (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom
    Flat p ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation p ∧
      ∀ s : S, GeometricallyReduced (p.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
        GeometricallyConnected (p.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.H (Scheme.structureSheafAb (p.fiber s)) 1)
